question: How many shipments were cancelled last quarter?
ai_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS cancelled_shipments
FROM shipments
WHERE status = 'Cancelled'
  AND created_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30';
ai_answer: There were 946 shipments cancelled last quarter. This count covers shipments created between July 1 and September 30, 2026, and includes only those with a status of Cancelled.

question: What % of UK shipments were held at customs?
ai_sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.hold_reason = 'At Customs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
             / COUNT(*), 1) AS customs_hold_pct
FROM shipments s
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = s.shipper_id
WHERE sh.country = 'UK'
  AND s.status <> 'Cancelled';
ai_answer: About 8.5% of UK shipments were held at customs. This covers all recorded shipments from UK shippers, with no date limit, and cancelled shipments were excluded from the count.

question: Compare on-time rate and cost per package for milkrun vs direct, last quarter.
ai_sql:
WITH run_costs AS (
    -- all truck runs in the period, including wasted runs
    SELECT run_type,
           SUM(cost_eur) AS total_cost_eur
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY run_type
),
shipment_stats AS (
    -- non-cancelled shipments on runs in the period, aggregated per run type
    SELECT tr.run_type,
           COUNT(*) AS shipments,
           SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivered_to_node_date IS NOT NULL
                     AND s.delivered_to_node_date <= s.promised_date
                    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_shipments,
           SUM(s.packages) AS packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
      AND tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY tr.run_type
)
SELECT ss.run_type,
       ss.shipments,
       ROUND(100.0 * ss.on_time_shipments / ss.shipments, 1) AS on_time_pct,
       ss.packages,
       ROUND(rc.total_cost_eur, 2) AS total_cost_eur,
       ROUND(rc.total_cost_eur / ss.packages, 2) AS cost_per_package_eur
FROM shipment_stats ss
JOIN run_costs rc ON rc.run_type = ss.run_type
ORDER BY ss.run_type;
ai_answer: Direct shipments were more often on time than milk runs: 87.8% versus 72.6%. Milk runs were cheaper per package, at €2.67 compared with €4.88 for direct. This covers July 1 to September 30, 2026, and excludes cancelled shipments; the cost figures include all truck runs in that period, including runs that carried no shipments.

question: What was our weekly attainment for FR shippers last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    -- aggregate actual volume to shipper x pickup day BEFORE joining (no fan-out)
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
fc AS (
    -- forecast rows for FR shippers, tagged with their Sunday-based week
    SELECT f.shipper_id, f.forecast_date, f.forecast_packages,
           date(f.forecast_date, '-' || strftime('%w', f.forecast_date) || ' days') AS week_start
    FROM forecasts f
    JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = f.shipper_id
    WHERE sh.country = 'FR'
),
daily AS (
    -- only days that have a forecast row count
    SELECT fc.week_start, fc.forecast_packages, COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages
    FROM fc
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = fc.shipper_id AND a.pickup_date = fc.forecast_date
)
SELECT week_start,
       SUM(forecast_packages) AS forecast_packages,
       SUM(actual_packages) AS actual_packages,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(actual_packages) / SUM(forecast_packages), 1) AS attainment_pct
FROM daily
WHERE week_start BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY week_start
ORDER BY week_start;
ai_answer:
FR shipper attainment ran between 95.9% and 98.9% each week from July 1 to September 30, 2026. The best week started July 5 at 98.9%, and the weakest started August 16 at 95.9%. Every week came in under 100%, so actual packages fell short of forecast throughout the quarter.

Weeks run Sunday to Saturday, so the week of June 28 is excluded and the week of July 5 is the first one counted. The final week (starting September 27) only covers the days through September 30, which is why its volume is smaller.

question: Which 10 shippers had the lowest attainment in Q3 2026?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
q3 AS (
    SELECT f.shipper_id,
           SUM(f.forecast_packages) AS forecast_total,
           SUM(COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0)) AS actual_total
    FROM forecasts f
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND a.pickup_date = f.forecast_date
    WHERE f.forecast_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY f.shipper_id
)
SELECT q.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       q.forecast_total,
       q.actual_total,
       ROUND(100.0 * q.actual_total / q.forecast_total, 1) AS attainment_pct
FROM q3 q
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = q.shipper_id
WHERE q.forecast_total >= 500
ORDER BY attainment_pct ASC
LIMIT 10;
ai_answer: The 10 shippers with the lowest attainment in Q3 2026 (forecast dates July 1 to September 30, 2026) ranged from 65.0% to 69.3%. Turner, Ford and Dobson was lowest at 65.0% (2,893 packages shipped against 4,450 forecast), followed by Bruneau at 65.1% and Desarrollo Globales S.L.N.E at 66.4%. Only shippers with at least 500 forecast packages were included, and cancelled shipments were excluded from actuals.

question: Did any de-listed shipper have volume after being de-listed?
ai_sql:
SELECT sh.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       sh.delisted_date,
       COUNT(DISTINCT tr.run_id) AS runs_after_delisting,
       SUM(s.packages) AS packages_after_delisting,
       MAX(tr.run_date) AS last_pickup_date
FROM shippers sh
JOIN shipments s ON s.shipper_id = sh.shipper_id
JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
WHERE sh.status = 'de-listed'
  AND sh.delisted_date IS NOT NULL
  AND s.status <> 'Cancelled'
  AND tr.run_date > sh.delisted_date
GROUP BY sh.shipper_id, sh.name, sh.delisted_date
ORDER BY packages_after_delisting DESC;
ai_answer: No de-listed shipper had any pickups after their de-listing date. The check covered all de-listed shippers that have a recorded de-listing date, all time periods, and excluded cancelled shipments. Any shipper that was de-listed and still shipped would have appeared in this check, so none did.

question: What was average truck utilisation by country last month?
ai_sql:
SELECT n.country,
       COUNT(*) AS truck_runs,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(tr.pallets_loaded) / SUM(tr.pallet_capacity), 1) AS utilisation_pct
FROM truck_runs tr
JOIN nodes n ON n.node_id = tr.node_id
WHERE tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY n.country
ORDER BY n.country;
ai_answer: Truck utilisation in September 2026 was similar across all four countries: UK was highest at 71.2%, followed by ES at 71.0%, IT at 70.9%, and FR lowest at 70.6%. This covers all truck runs dated 1 to 30 September 2026, grouped by the country of the node each run is tied to. Utilisation is total pallets loaded divided by total pallet capacity, so it weights the overall load rather than averaging per-run percentages.

question: Which nodes went over capacity during peak 2025, and on how many days?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_load AS (
    -- node load = pallets loaded on runs arriving at the node, per pickup (run) date
    SELECT node_id, run_date, SUM(pallets_loaded) AS load_pallets
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_date BETWEEN '2025-11-28' AND '2025-12-24'
    GROUP BY node_id, run_date
)
SELECT n.node_id,
       n.city,
       n.country,
       n.daily_capacity_pallets,
       COUNT(*) AS days_over_capacity,
       MAX(dl.load_pallets) AS peak_day_load_pallets
FROM daily_load dl
JOIN nodes n ON n.node_id = dl.node_id
WHERE dl.load_pallets > n.daily_capacity_pallets
GROUP BY n.node_id, n.city, n.country, n.daily_capacity_pallets
ORDER BY days_over_capacity DESC, peak_day_load_pallets DESC;
ai_answer: Only one node went over capacity during the peak window: London, UK (node N-UK-01), which exceeded its 150-pallet daily capacity on 19 days. Its heaviest day loaded 253 pallets. The count covers pickup dates from 28 November to 24 December 2025, and it includes all runs arriving at each node.

question: Which Account Managers' shippers drove the most avoidable cost last quarter?
ai_sql:
WITH run_avoidable AS (
    -- avoidable cost per run: wasted-truck cost + ad-hoc premium (both parts)
    SELECT tr.run_id,
           (CASE WHEN tr.run_outcome = 'wasted' THEN tr.cost_eur ELSE 0 END
          + CASE WHEN tr.is_adhoc = 1 THEN tr.cost_eur * 0.6 / 1.6 ELSE 0 END) AS avoidable_eur
    FROM truck_runs tr
    WHERE tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
),
stop_counts AS (
    SELECT run_id, COUNT(*) AS n_stops
    FROM run_stops
    GROUP BY run_id
)
SELECT s.account_manager,
       ROUND(SUM(ra.avoidable_eur / sc.n_stops), 2) AS avoidable_cost_eur
FROM run_avoidable ra
JOIN stop_counts sc ON sc.run_id = ra.run_id
JOIN run_stops rs   ON rs.run_id = ra.run_id          -- split cost equally across stops
JOIN shippers s     ON s.shipper_id = rs.shipper_id
GROUP BY s.account_manager
ORDER BY avoidable_cost_eur DESC;
ai_answer: **Denis Davies's shippers drove the most avoidable cost, at €21,625.74**, followed by Alphonse Durand (€19,988.22) and Angelica Santi (€17,452.26). The figures cover truck runs dated 1 July to 30 September 2026, and avoidable cost means the cost of runs that were wasted plus the premium paid on ad-hoc runs. Each run's cost is split equally across the shippers it served.

question: How much unplanned volume did we get on bank holidays in 2026, by country?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    -- aggregate actual volume to shipper x pickup day BEFORE joining (no fan-out)
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
      AND tr.run_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-12-31'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
)
SELECT sh.country,
       SUM(a.actual_packages) AS unplanned_packages,
       COUNT(*) AS unplanned_shipper_days
FROM daily_actual a
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = a.shipper_id
WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM holidays h
        WHERE h.country = sh.country
          AND h.holiday_date = a.pickup_date
      )
  AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM forecasts f
        WHERE f.shipper_id = a.shipper_id
          AND f.forecast_date = a.pickup_date
      )
GROUP BY sh.country
ORDER BY sh.country;
ai_answer: In 2026, unplanned volume on bank holidays was 1,763 packages in Spain (44 shipper-days), 3,402 in France (82 shipper-days), 2,285 in Italy (54 shipper-days), and 2,900 in the UK (66 shipper-days). "Unplanned" means shipper-days with no forecast on that day, and cancelled shipments are excluded. Each country's count uses that country's own holiday calendar.

question: Which shippers missed the +/-10% attainment band for 3+ consecutive weeks?
ai_sql:
WITH daily_actual AS (
    -- aggregate actual volume to shipper x pickup day BEFORE joining (no fan-out)
    SELECT s.shipper_id, tr.run_date AS pickup_date, SUM(s.packages) AS actual_packages
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = s.run_id
    WHERE s.status <> 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY s.shipper_id, tr.run_date
),
daily AS (
    -- forecast side drives the join; only days with a forecast row count
    SELECT f.shipper_id, f.forecast_date, f.forecast_packages,
           COALESCE(a.actual_packages, 0) AS actual_packages
    FROM forecasts f
    LEFT JOIN daily_actual a
      ON a.shipper_id = f.shipper_id AND a.pickup_date = f.forecast_date
),
weekly AS (
    -- Sunday-start weeks labelled by their Sunday date
    SELECT shipper_id,
           date(forecast_date, '-' || strftime('%w', forecast_date) || ' days') AS week_start,
           SUM(forecast_packages) AS fc,
           SUM(actual_packages) AS act
    FROM daily
    GROUP BY shipper_id, week_start
),
missed AS (
    -- weeks outside the 90%-110% band, with a gaps-and-islands key for consecutiveness
    SELECT shipper_id, week_start,
           julianday(week_start) - 7 * ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY shipper_id ORDER BY week_start) AS grp
    FROM weekly
    WHERE fc > 0
      AND (1.0 * act / fc < 0.9 OR 1.0 * act / fc > 1.1)
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT shipper_id, MIN(week_start) AS start_week, MAX(week_start) AS end_week,
           COUNT(*) AS missed_weeks
    FROM missed
    GROUP BY shipper_id, grp
)
SELECT st.shipper_id, sh.name, st.start_week, st.end_week, st.missed_weeks
FROM streaks st
JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = st.shipper_id
WHERE st.missed_weeks >= 3
ORDER BY st.missed_weeks DESC, st.shipper_id;
ai_answer: There were 366 runs of at least three consecutive weeks where a shipper's actual volume fell outside the ±10% band of its forecast. The count covers weeks starting Sunday from 2024-12-29 through 2026-09-27, excluding cancelled shipments. The longest runs are 12 shippers each missing 92 weeks in a row (2024-12-29 to 2026-09-27), which may point to a forecast or data-loading problem rather than real performance. Next are Webb, Shaw and Pritchard (11 weeks, 2025-11-30 to 2026-02-08) and Allen, Smith and Jones (10 weeks, 2025-12-21 to 2026-02-22), and only the first 50 of the 366 runs are shown.

question: For milkruns, which shippers are most often the cause of late node arrivals?
ai_sql:
WITH stop_late AS (
    -- pickup lateness per stop, in minutes, plus the previous stop's lateness on the same run
    SELECT rs.run_id, rs.shipper_id, rs.stop_sequence,
           (julianday(rs.actual_pickup_time) - julianday(rs.planned_pickup_time)) * 1440.0 AS lateness,
           LAG((julianday(rs.actual_pickup_time) - julianday(rs.planned_pickup_time)) * 1440.0)
               OVER (PARTITION BY rs.run_id ORDER BY rs.stop_sequence) AS prev_lateness
    FROM run_stops rs
),
stop_delay AS (
    -- delay added by each stop = its lateness minus the previous stop's lateness
    SELECT run_id, shipper_id, stop_sequence,
           lateness - COALESCE(prev_lateness, 0) AS delay_added
    FROM stop_late
),
late_milkruns AS (
    -- completed milkruns that arrived late at the node
    SELECT run_id
    FROM truck_runs
    WHERE run_type = 'milkrun'
      AND run_outcome = 'completed'
      AND actual_arrival_time > planned_arrival_time
),
blamed AS (
    -- for each late milkrun, the stop that added the most delay is blamed
    SELECT sd.run_id, sd.shipper_id,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sd.run_id
                              ORDER BY sd.delay_added DESC, sd.stop_sequence) AS rn
    FROM stop_delay sd
    JOIN late_milkruns lm ON lm.run_id = sd.run_id
),
milkrun_counts AS (
    -- total milkruns each shipper appears on
    SELECT rs.shipper_id, COUNT(DISTINCT rs.run_id) AS milkruns
    FROM run_stops rs
    JOIN truck_runs tr ON tr.run_id = rs.run_id
    WHERE tr.run_type = 'milkrun'
    GROUP BY rs.shipper_id
)
SELECT b.shipper_id,
       sh.name,
       COUNT(*) AS late_milkruns_blamed,
       mc.milkruns
FROM blamed b
JOIN milkrun_counts mc ON mc.shipper_id = b.shipper_id
LEFT JOIN shippers sh ON sh.shipper_id = b.shipper_id
WHERE b.rn = 1
  AND mc.milkruns >= 20
GROUP BY b.shipper_id, sh.name, mc.milkruns
ORDER BY late_milkruns_blamed DESC;
ai_answer: Adam 453 is the shipper most often blamed for late milkrun node arrivals, with 185 late milkruns out of the 191 it appeared on. The next highest were Anichini-Zabarella SPA 579 (178 of 183) and Ferrand 496 (171 of 177). The analysis covers all completed milkruns in the data that arrived after their planned time, with no date range applied. A shipper is blamed when its stop added the most delay to that run, and only shippers on at least 20 milkruns are included.
